mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In rising rate regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) using a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) suggests weakening labor market strength and disinflation, which tends to boost S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in one month while CPIAUCSL decreases by at least 1% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening with deflationary signals
failure_condition: Over 20-day horizon, returns are negative or flat despite the trigger, with a p-value > 0.05 in a regression controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in housing starts (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from inventory-driven to demand-driven economic expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 15% in one month while INDPRO decreases by at least 5% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from soft to firm demand
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) after controlling for macroeconomic risk factors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints that reduce expected corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) turns positive after two consecutive months of declines, it signals the end of deflationary pressures and typically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months then increases in the third month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative, with a p-value > 0.05 in a regression including FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% for a month suggests labor market weakness that lowers growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by at least 0.5 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) despite the UNRATE increase.
